18		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/contexts"
19		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/httpclient"
20		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/repocreds"
21		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper"
22		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/debuglog"
23		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/githelper"
24		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/replicas"
25		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/transport"
26	)
27	
28	// invokedAsRemoteHelper reports whether this process was launched under
29	// the git-remote-entire name (via the shipped symlink/copy). Detection is
30	// by argv[0] basename, with a Windows .exe suffix tolerated. Git resolves
31	// `entire://` URLs by exec'ing remotehelper.BinaryName on PATH, so a single
32	// binary serves both roles (busybox/git style).
33	func invokedAsRemoteHelper(arg0 string) bool {
34		base := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(arg0), ".exe")
35		return base == remotehelper.BinaryName
36	}
37	
38	// runRemoteHelper implements the git remote-helper protocol for
39	// `entire://` URLs. Git invokes us as `git-remote-entire <remote> <url>`,
40	// hands us the helper protocol on stdin, and expects responses on stdout.
41	//
42	// IMPORTANT: nothing on this path may write to stdout except the helper
43	// protocol itself — git parses stdout as a strict pkt-line stream, so a
44	// stray banner or log line corrupts the transfer. Diagnostics go to
45	// stderr (and the ENTIRE_DEBUG-gated debuglog).
46	//
47	// Authentication resolves the login context for the target cluster from
48	// the shared contexts.json (honoring an explicit cluster binding, else
49	// /.well-known discovery), then mints repo-scoped tokens by exchanging
50	// that context's login JWT. A pre-contexts.json login is migrated in
51	// read-time so existing users don't have to re-authenticate.
52	func runRemoteHelper(args []string) int {
53		if len(args) < 3 {
54			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: git-remote-entire <remote-name> <url>")
55			return 128
56		}
57	
58		// Build info drives the agent string the helper advertises upstream.
59		versioninfo.Load()
60		githelper.Agent = remotehelper.BinaryName + "/" + versioninfo.Commit
61	
62		rawURL := args[2]
63		parsedURL, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
64		switch {
65		case err != nil:
66			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: invalid URL %q: %v\n", rawURL, err)
67			return 128
68		case parsedURL.Scheme != "entire":
69			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: unsupported URL scheme %q (expected 'entire')\n", parsedURL.Scheme)
70			return 128
71		case parsedURL.Host == "":
72			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: missing host in URL %q\n", rawURL)
73			return 128
74		}
75	
76		ctx, stop := installRemoteHelperSignals()
77		defer stop()
78	
79		skipTLS := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY") == "true"
80	
81		nodeCfg := replicas.Resolve(parsedURL)
82		// The repo-scoped token's audience is <clusterBaseURL><repoSlug>. The
83		// audience pins to the cluster entry URL (not a replica node), matching
84		// what the server validates the exchanged token against.
85		clusterBaseURL := nodeCfg.EntryURL
86		repoSlug := parsedURL.Path
87	
88		httpClient := &http.Client{
89			Timeout:   30 * time.Second,
90			Transport: httpclient.NewTransport(skipTLS),
91		}
92	
93		// Bridge any pre-contexts.json login so the resolver can find it.
94		if _, err := auth.MigrateLegacyLoginContext(); err != nil {
95			debuglog.Printf("legacy login migration: %v", err)
96		}
97	
98		// Resolve which login context authenticates this cluster: an explicit
99		// cluster_contexts binding wins, otherwise the cluster's
100		// /.well-known/entire-cluster.json is matched against local contexts.
101		cfgDir := contexts.DefaultConfigDir()
102		clusterCtx, err := clusterdiscovery.ResolveContextForCluster(ctx, cfgDir, parsedURL.Host, httpClient, debuglog.Printf)
103		if err != nil {
104			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: %v\n", err)
105			return 128
106		}
107	
108		// Mint repo-scoped tokens by exchanging the context's login JWT at its
109		// core's /oauth/token, cached per (repo, action) for this invocation.
110		creds := repocreds.New(clusterCtx.CoreURL, clusterBaseURL, func(context.Context) (string, error) {
111			return auth.LoginTokenForContext(clusterCtx)
112		}, httpClient)
113	
114		setAuth := func(req *http.Request) error {
115			action := gitActionFromRequest(req)
116			if action == "" {
117				return fmt.Errorf("cannot classify git op for %s %s; scoped-token exchange requires a recognised smart-HTTP endpoint", req.Method, req.URL.Path)
118			}
119			token, err := creds.Token(req.Context(), repoSlug, action)
120			if err != nil {
121				return fmt.Errorf("repo-scoped token exchange: %w", err)
122			}
123			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
124			return nil
125		}
126	
127		var onNodeFailed func(string)
128		if nodeCfg.Caching() {
129			onNodeFailed = func(string) { replicas.Invalidate(nodeCfg.ClusterHost, nodeCfg.RepoPath) }
130		}
131	
132		proxy := transport.New(transport.Config{
133			Nodes:        nodeCfg,
134			Path:         parsedURL.Path,
135			SkipTLS:      skipTLS,
136			SetAuth:      setAuth,
137			OnNodeFailed: onNodeFailed,
138		})
139	
140		mode := githelper.ModeConnect
141		if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_STATELESS") == "true" {
142			mode = githelper.ModeStateless
143		}
144	
145		if err := githelper.Run(ctx, proxy, mode, os.Stdin, os.Stdout); err != nil {
146			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: %v\n", err)
147			return 128
148		}
149		return 0
150	}
151	
152	// gitActionFromRequest classifies a smart-HTTP request as "pull" or
153	// "push" so the right repo-scoped token can be minted. Returns "" when
154	// the endpoint isn't a recognised git smart-HTTP route.
155	func gitActionFromRequest(req *http.Request) string {
156		path := req.URL.Path
157		switch req.Method {
158		case http.MethodPost:
159			switch {
160			case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/git-receive-pack"):
161				return "push"
162			case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/git-upload-pack"):
163				return "pull"
164			}
165		case http.MethodGet:
166			if strings.HasSuffix(path, "/info/refs") {
167				switch req.URL.Query().Get("service") {
168				case "git-receive-pack":
169					return "push"
170				case "git-upload-pack":
171					return "pull"
172				}
173			}
174		}
175		return ""
176	}
177	
178	// installRemoteHelperSignals ties HTTP request lifetimes to the parent
179	// git process. Ctrl-C delivers SIGINT to the whole foreground process
180	// group (us included); cancelling ctx aborts in-flight transfers instead
181	// of waiting out the read timeout. After the first signal we unhook so a
182	// second Ctrl-C hits the runtime default and hard-exits.
183	func installRemoteHelperSignals() (context.Context, context.CancelFunc) {
184		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
185		go func() {
186			<-ctx.Done()
187			stop()
188			time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
189			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "git-remote-entire: shutdown taking longer than expected; press Ctrl-C again to force-quit")
190		}()
191		return ctx, stop
192	}

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema-pro.json
version: 2
pro: true

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - mise run completions

builds:
  - main: ./cmd/entire
    binary: entire
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Commit={{.ShortCommit}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry.PostHogAPIKey={{.Env.POSTHOG_API_KEY}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry.PostHogEndpoint={{.Env.POSTHOG_ENDPOINT}}

notarize:
  macos:
    - enabled: '{{ isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12" }}'
      sign:
        certificate: "{{.Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12}}"
        password: "{{.Env.MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD}}"
      notarize:
        issuer_id: "{{.Env.MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID}}"
        key_id: "{{.Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID}}"
        key: "{{.Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY}}"
        wait: true # do not let an unusable binary slip into the wild

archives:
  - formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    name_template: "entire_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - src: completions/*
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: LICENSE
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: README.md
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"

release:
  prerelease: auto

scoops:
  - repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: scoop-bucket
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/cli"
    description: "CLI for Entire"
    license: MIT
    skip_upload: auto

homebrew_casks:
  - name: entire
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/cli"
    description: "CLI for Entire"
    binaries:
      - entire
    generate_completions_from_executable:
      executable: entire
      shell_parameter_format: cobra
      shells:
        - bash
        - zsh
        - fish
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire@nightly
    skip_upload: auto

  - name: entire@nightly
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/cli"
    description: "CLI for Entire (nightly build)"
    binaries:
      - entire
    generate_completions_from_executable:
      executable: entire
      shell_parameter_format: cobra
      shells:
        - bash
        - zsh
        - fish
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire
    skip_upload: "{{ if not .Prerelease }}true{{ end }}"

announce:
  discord:
    enabled: '{{ and (not .Prerelease) (isEnvSet "DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ID") (isEnvSet "DISCORD_WEBHOOK_TOKEN") }}'

Fixed and verified — `c31fba3e2` is coherent and builds (the broken deletions-only commit was amended). Working tree clean, no stray stashes.

## Two-binary refactor — done

Switched from the argv[0]-symlink model to a **dedicated lean `git-remote-entire` binary** shipped on every channel:

- **`cmd/git-remote-entire`** — new lean main running the helper loop directly; imports only the protocol + auth packages (no cobra tree). **~28 MB stripped** vs the full CLI's ~45 MB, so far cheaper than shipping `entire` twice. Logic moved verbatim — behavior unchanged. Added a unit test for the action classifier.
- **Removed** the argv[0] dispatch (`cmd/entire/remotehelper.go` deleted, `main.go` branch gone) and all the install-time symlink machinery (`EnsureGitRemoteHelper`, the post-install hook).
- **`.goreleaser.yaml`** — second build (`id: git-remote-entire`, versioninfo stamp only, no telemetry) + listed in both Homebrew casks' `binaries:`. Standard goreleaser fields (multiple builds need explicit `id`s; cask `binaries` is a plain list), so much lower risk than the hook hacks I'd otherwise have needed.
- **`install.sh`** — installs both binaries from the archive.

**Why this nails Windows + scoop:** because `git-remote-entire`'s `main()` *always* runs the helper, it no longer depends on `argv[0]` at all. So even if scoop's shim execs the target with a rewritten `argv[0]`, it still works — the entire class of shim/symlink/elevation problems disappears. That was your insight, and it's the decisive reason this is the better pattern.

**Verified:** unit **5939**, integration **352**, canary **59+4**, lint clean (no `--fix`) on changed packages, shellcheck clean. Both binaries build and behave.

One honest caveat unchanged from before: I still can't run `goreleaser check` offline (it's pro + needs a key), so the release config wants a `goreleaser check` / snapshot pass before the next release — but these are core fields, not exotic ones.

1	# Entire - CLI
2	
3	This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8	
9	## Key Directories
10	
11	### Commands (`cmd/`)
12	
13	- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
14	- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
15	- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16	- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17	- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18	- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
19	- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20	- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21	- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22	
23	### Command Layout
24	
25	The CLI is organized around five noun groups plus a small set of top-level
26	verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb; legacy top-level
27	shortcuts remain functional but hidden, and emit a deprecation hint pointing
28	at the canonical group form.
29	
30	- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `stop`, `attach`, `resume`, `current`
31	- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `rewind`, `search`

133	
134	```go
135	func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
136	    t.Parallel()
137	    // ...

159	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
160	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG
161	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "f.txt", "init")  // create a file
162	testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "f.txt")             // stage it
163	testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")           // commit (needs at least one commit for HEAD)
164	t.Chdir(tmpDir)                                 // redirect CWD-based git resolution
165	```

1. [high] Multi-context login still collapses same-core accounts into one entry
     - RecordLoginContext always derives the context name from contextNameForCoreURL(coreURL) (cmd/entire/cli/auth/contexts.go:67,151), and Upsert replaces any existing context with
       the same name (internal/entireclient/contexts/contexts.go:170).
     - That means logging into the same core as a second user overwrites the first context instead of creating another one. So the new “multi-context auth” flow still can’t actually
       store multiple identities for one issuer.
 2. [high] entire auth revoke does not honor context-backed logins
     - newAuthRevokeCmd wires runAuthRevoke to auth.NewStore() instead of auth.NewContextStore() (cmd/entire/cli/auth.go:477-500).
     - As a result, users who are “logged in” only via contexts.json (for example, after switching contexts or after a login created by another CLI) get not logged in from entire
       auth revoke --current. Even worse, when revoking by ID, the cleanup path only deletes the legacy keyring entry, leaving the active context token in place
       (cmd/entire/cli/auth.go:517+).
 3. [medium] Running the git helper can unexpectedly switch the user’s active CLI context
     - git-remote-entire calls auth.MigrateLegacyLoginContext() on startup (cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:81).
     - If migration is needed, it calls RecordLoginContext, which unconditionally sets f.CurrentContext = name (cmd/entire/cli/auth/contexts.go:69-79).
     - So a first git clone entire://... after upgrade can silently change current_context, altering which account later control-plane commands run under. Migration should preserve
       the existing current context when one is already set.

content.text:
All three review findings are fixed, committed (`e1f1b3ec0`), and pushed to PR #1306.

## Summary of the fixes

**#1 — same-core accounts no longer collapse.** `RecordLoginContext` now keys on **identity (core URL + handle)**: re-logging into the same identity updates its context in place, but a second identity on the same core gets its own context named `handle@host` instead of clobbering the first via `Upsert`. (`pickContextName` handles the bare-host → `handle@host` → numeric-suffix progression.)

**#2 — `auth revoke` honors context-backed logins.** The command now uses `auth.NewContextStore()` (so `revoke --current` sees a context-only login), and the by-ID self-revoke path — when it detects via 401 that it revoked this CLI's own token — clears the **active context** too, not just the legacy keyring entry. The context-clear is threaded as a `clearContext` func, mirroring `logout`.

**#3 — migration no longer hijacks the active context.** `RecordLoginContext` gained an `activate` flag: `entire login` passes `true` (kubectl use-context semantics), but the git helper's read-time `MigrateLegacyLoginContext` passes `false` — so a first `git clone entire://…` after upgrade records the legacy context without silently switching `current_context`. It still sets `current` when none exists yet.

**Tests added:** same-core coexistence + re-login-in-place (#1), and migration preserving an already-active context (#3). All call sites updated for the new signatures.

**Verified:** full unit (5886), integration (348), e2e canary (59+4) green; `golangci-lint` clean (no `--fix`) on the changed packages.

PR #1306 now has the follow-up commit on top of the rebased stack.

     - ResolveContextForCluster takes matches := f.ContextsForIssuer(coreURL) and then blindly uses matches[0] in internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go.
     - After this branch, same-core multi-user contexts are supported (alice@core, bob@core), but first clone against a new cluster will auto-bind whichever one was saved first, not
       the active context.
     - Result: git clone entire://... can silently authenticate as the wrong user.
 2. [medium] Legacy-login migration skips same-core/different-user identities
     - MigrateLegacyLoginContext bails out when len(f.ContextsForIssuer(claims.Issuer)) > 0 in cmd/entire/cli/auth/contexts.go.
     - That only checks issuer, not (issuer, handle).
     - If contexts.json already has alice@core from another CLI, but the legacy entire keyring token is bob@core, migration is skipped and Bob never gets a context.
 3. [medium] User-facing auth errors point at the wrong CLI/command
     - internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/discovery.go tells users to run entire-core auth login --base-url <url>.
     - internal/remotehelper/transport/inforefs.go says please run 'entire-core auth login'.
     - This repo ships entire, not entire-core, and login here is not a --base-url command. So the recovery instructions are misleading.
 4. [medium] Replica cache updates are still racy across processes
     - internal/remotehelper/replicas/Persist and Invalidate do LoadCache → mutate → SaveCache.
     - SaveCache locks only the write; the whole read-modify-write sequence is not atomic.
     - Two concurrent clone/fetch/push processes can overwrite each other’s nodes.json updates and lose cache entries. This is the same class of race contexts.Modify(...) was added
       to avoid.

12	// ResolveContextForCluster picks the auth context for clusterHost.
13	// Resolution order:
14	//
15	//  1. Explicit `cluster_contexts[clusterHost]` binding in contexts.json
16	//     pointing at an existing context — used as-is.
17	//  2. Discovery via /.well-known/entire-cluster.json on the cluster
18	//     itself, matched against existing local contexts by the
19	//     advertised core_urls. The first advertised URL with a local
20	//     context wins, and the cluster→context binding is written so the
21	//     next call skips discovery.
22	//  3. No local context matches any advertised URL — return a
23	//     fatal-ready error with the login hint listing the cluster's
24	//     advertised issuers.
25	//
26	// We deliberately do NOT fall back to current_context for an unknown
27	// cluster host. The old fallback would silently use a staging
28	// context against a prod (entire.io) cluster — which
29	// then 400s as "unknown cluster_host" because the cluster's own
30	// registry doesn't know the host. The cluster's /.well-known is the
31	// authoritative answer to "which env am I in", so we ask it.
32	//
33	// debugf is optional; nil suppresses debug output.
34	func ResolveContextForCluster(ctx context.Context, configDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) (*contexts.Context, error) {
35		if debugf == nil {
36			debugf = func(string, ...any) {}
37		}
38		f, err := contexts.Load(configDir)
39		if err != nil {
40			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load contexts: %w", err)
41		}
42		if name, ok := f.ClusterContexts[clusterHost]; ok && name != "" {
43			if c := f.Find(name); c != nil {
44				debugf("contexts.json binding %s -> %s", clusterHost, c.Name)
45				return c, nil
46			}
47			debugf("stale binding %s -> %q (context no longer exists); falling through to discovery", clusterHost, name)
48		}
49		body, err := Discover(ctx, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, formatDiscoveryError(clusterHost, err)
52		}
53		for _, coreURL := range body.CoreURLs {
54			matches := f.ContextsForIssuer(coreURL)
55			if len(matches) == 0 {
56				continue
57			}
58			c := matches[0]
59			if bindErr := contexts.BindCluster(configDir, clusterHost, c.Name); bindErr != nil {
60				// Non-fatal: we still resolved a usable context. Next
61				// invocation will pay the discovery round-trip again.
62				debugf("auto-bind %s -> %s failed: %v", clusterHost, c.Name, bindErr)
63			} else {
64				debugf("auto-bound %s -> %s after discovery match on %s", clusterHost, c.Name, coreURL)
65			}
66			return c, nil
67		}
68		return nil, errors.New(RenderLoginHint(clusterHost, body.CoreURLs))
69	}
70	
71	// formatDiscoveryError turns a Discover error into the message
72	// operators have always seen at this layer. Kept here (not on the
73	// sentinels themselves) so the package's errors stay machine-readable
74	// while the caller-facing strings remain centralised.
75	func formatDiscoveryError(clusterHost string, err error) error {
76		switch {
77		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnreachable):
78			return fmt.Errorf("%s doesn't look like a cluster, or it is unreachable: %w", clusterHost, err)
79		case errors.Is(err, ErrNoIssuers):
80			return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s does not advertise any trusted login servers (HTTP 503 from %s); contact the cluster administrator",
81				clusterHost, Path)
82		case errors.Is(err, ErrNoCoreURLs):
83			return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s advertises no trusted core URLs (empty list at %s); contact the cluster administrator",
84				clusterHost, Path)
85		default:
86			return fmt.Errorf("cluster discovery for %s: %w", clusterHost, err)
87		}
88	}

content.text:
All four findings are fixed, committed (`7c97a7f54`), and pushed to PR #1306.

## Summary

**#1 [high] — wrong-account on new-cluster resolve.** `ResolveContextForCluster` blindly took `matches[0]` among an issuer's contexts. It now **prefers `current_context`** when it's one of the eligible matches (falling back to the first otherwise), so a core with `alice@core`/`bob@core` auto-binds to the active account, not whichever was saved first.

**#2 [medium] — migration skipped same-core/different-user.** `MigrateLegacyLoginContext` bailed when *any* context existed for the issuer. It now skips only when the **exact `(issuer, handle)` identity** is already represented, so a legacy `bob@core` migrates even when `alice@core` exists.

**#3 [medium] — wrong CLI in error hints.** The cluster login hint and the info/refs 401 message referenced `entire-core auth login --base-url`. Both now point at `entire login` / `entire auth use <context>` — accurate for the binary this repo ships.

**#4 [medium] — racy replica cache.** Added `discovery.ModifyCache` (load-mutate-save under a single flock, mirroring `contexts.Modify`); `replicas.Persist`/`Invalidate` use it instead of the non-atomic `LoadCache → mutate → SaveCache`, so concurrent clone/fetch/push no longer clobber `nodes.json`.

**Tests added:** prefer-current resolution, same-core different-handle migration, `ModifyCache` atomicity + abort-on-error, plus updated hint assertions. Full unit (5888), integration (348), canary (59+4) green; `golangci-lint` clean (no `--fix`).

I noted in the commit that the `clusterdiscovery`/`discovery`/`replicas` edits are in **vendored** packages — these fixes (especially #1, #4) are worth upstreaming to entiredb and should be reconciled in the planned auth-go extraction (entiredb likely has the same `matches[0]` and cache-race bugs).

Also cleaned up a stale-cache lint fluke along the way (an `ireturn` nolint in `tokenstore.go` briefly flagged as unused) — reverted to the original, confirmed clean.

content.text:
These are sharp findings. Let me give you my honest read on each — they're all real, but they're not the same *kind* of problem.

## #2 — logout silently switches accounts — **real bug, clean fix**

`File.Delete` advancing `current_context` to the first survivor is the right behavior for a *context delete* command, but it's wrong for **logout**. "Logged out" must mean *not authenticated*, not "now you're someone else." Worse, it's a quiet security footgun — you think you logged out but you're still authed as another identity.

Fix is small and unambiguous: in `RemoveCurrentContext`, after `f.Delete`, **clear `current_context`** rather than letting it advance. (Single-context logout is unchanged; only the multi-context case stops silently switching.) I'm confident in this one.

## #3 — login hint not actionable for non-default cores — **real, fixable**

You're right that `entire login` always targets `api.AuthBaseURL()`. But it *does* honor `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` — so the actionable recovery for a cluster that accepts a *different* core is `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=<one-of-those-urls> entire login`. The hint should say that (or "switch to an existing context on one of these with `entire auth use`"). That's accurate and unblocks the user. Clean fix.

## #1 — `auth use` doesn't retarget the control plane across cores — **real, and the deep one**

This is correctly diagnosed and it's the important one. The root cause: `auth use` only moves the *token* (`ContextStore.LoadTokens`), but the control-plane **host/issuer** is process-wide — `defaultManager` pins `Issuer = api.AuthBaseURL()` and the coreapi client targets `api.BaseURL()`. Neither follows the active context's `CoreURL`.

The crucial nuance: this is **fine for same-core multi-user** (`alice@core`/`bob@core` — same issuer, only the token differs, which works), and it's **fine for clone** (the git helper builds `repocreds` from `clusterCtx.CoreURL` per-invocation, so clone already resolves per-context correctly). It's **only broken for control-plane commands switching across *different cores*** (staging↔prod, self-hosted, etc.).

And a partial fix would be *worse*: I could make `defaultManager` derive the issuer from the current context, but the **data API host** (`api.BaseURL`) also has to move with it — and the context only stores `CoreURL` (the issuer/auth host), with no per-context data host in this CLI's split-host model (`us.auth.entire.io` vs `entire.io`). So "issuer follows context but data host doesn't" gets you half-right, which is arguably worse than today. A *correct* fix is the broader **"control plane follows the active context"** work — per-context host resolution — which is exactly the multi-core control-plane piece I flagged as deferred (it pairs naturally with the auth-go extraction).

So for #1 my recommendation is: **make the feature honest now, do the full retarget later.** Concretely, the honest-now fix:
- `auth use` **warns** (or refuses) when the target context's `CoreURL` differs from the active control-plane auth host, stating that control-plane commands still target the configured host and that clone works per-context regardless;
- correct the over-promising docstring/help on `auth use` / `auth contexts`.

That prevents the silent wrong-host auth without shipping a half-correct retarget.

Here's the one real decision — #2 and #3 I'll just fix:

cd /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
auth: honest cross-core scoping, true logout, actionable login hint

Third round of review fixes for the multi-context flow:

1. `auth use` no longer over-claims cross-core control-plane switching.
   The active context only retargets which login `git clone entire://…`
   prefers; control-plane commands (auth status/list/revoke,
   org/project/repo/grant) still target the configured auth host
   (ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL / default) because the token manager and coreapi
   client are built against api.AuthBaseURL(), not the context's core. So
   `auth use` now warns when the target context authenticates against a
   different core, and the docs say so plainly. (Full per-context host
   resolution is the deferred multi-core control-plane work.)

2. Logout truly logs out. RemoveCurrentContext let File.Delete advance
   current_context to a surviving context, so `entire logout` (and `auth
   revoke --current`) silently re-authenticated as another account while
   printing "Logged out". It now clears current_context — logged out means
   logged out; other contexts survive and can be re-selected with
   `entire auth use`.

3. Cluster login hint is actionable for non-default cores. `entire login`
   only targets the configured host, so RenderLoginHint now suggests
   `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=<url> entire login` (or `entire auth use` for an
   existing login) so users can authenticate against a cluster's
   non-default accepted core.

Tests: cross-core warning (warns vs silent same-core), logout clears
current without switching, hint mentions ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL.
Full unit/integration/canary green; lint clean (no --fix).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
echo "EXIT=$?" && git log --oneline -1 && echo "=== push ===" && git push 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
All three fixed, committed (`653dbda0a`), and pushed to PR #1306. My take, recapped with what I did:

## #2 — logout switching accounts — **fixed (clean bug)**
`RemoveCurrentContext` now clears `current_context` after deleting, instead of letting `File.Delete` advance to a survivor. `entire logout` / `auth revoke --current` truly log out; other contexts survive for `entire auth use`. The security-footgun ("you think you logged out but you're someone else") is gone.

## #3 — login hint — **fixed (now actionable)**
`RenderLoginHint` now suggests `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=<url> entire login` (or `entire auth use` for an existing login on that core), since plain `entire login` only hits the configured host. Tests assert the env-var guidance is present.

## #1 — control plane not following the active context across cores — **honestly scoped now, full fix deferred**
This is the real architectural gap, and per your call I made the feature **honest rather than half-correct**: `auth use` now **warns** when the target context's core differs from the configured auth host (control-plane commands still target the configured host; clone uses the context regardless), and the docstrings/help no longer claim cross-core control-plane switching works. I deliberately did **not** ship a partial issuer-only retarget, because without a per-context data host it would be worse than today.

The genuine fix — control-plane host/issuer derived from the active context — remains the **multi-core control-plane** work that pairs with the auth-go extraction. That's now the cleanest single remaining item, and it'd want a per-context data-host model (this CLI is split-host, unlike entiredb where `CoreURL` is the single base).

**Verified:** unit 5891, integration 350, canary 59+4; lint clean (no `--fix`). All three findings have tests.

Net: PR #1306 has had three rounds of review fixes now. The known, documented remaining limitation is cross-core control-plane retargeting (#1's full fix) — everything else from the three review passes is resolved.

content.text:
Both are about the gap between messaging and the reality of `cluster_contexts` bindings. Let me give you my read, then implement.

**#1** is a clear wording bug — `cluster_contexts[host]` is resolved *first*, so for an already-bound cluster `auth use` is a no-op for clone. "uses this context regardless" is only true for unbound clusters. Fix: make the warning/docs accurate (binding wins; the active context only affects clusters not yet bound).

**#2** — my recommendation: **do both.** They're complementary and together make it honest:
- **Default `entire logout`** stays scoped (removes the active account, doesn't silently switch), but the message now **flags remaining logins** — because, as you note, surviving contexts + their cluster bindings can still authenticate clone/push. So "Logged out." overstates it.
- **Add `entire logout --all`** for the real "log me out everywhere" — removes every context, its token, and all cluster bindings.

That gives users an honest default *and* a one-shot full logout, rather than forcing a choice. Let me implement #1 + both halves of #2.

Both fixed, committed (`aa7a073eb`), and pushed to PR #1306.

## #1 — `auth use` overstated clone behavior — **fixed (wording)**
You're right: `ResolveContextForCluster` checks `cluster_contexts[host]` **first**, so for an already-bound cluster the active context is irrelevant to clone/push — "uses this context regardless" was only true for *unbound* clusters. The warning and the command help now say it accurately: **a bound cluster keeps its binding; the active context applies only to clusters not yet bound.**

## #2 — logout isn't a full logout — **did both, per your instinct**
Both, because they're complementary:

- **Default `entire logout`** stays scoped (removes the active account, no silent switch) but now **flags the survivors**: it lists the remaining saved logins and notes they can still authenticate clones, pointing at `--all` / `auth use`. So "Logged out." no longer overstates it.
- **`entire logout --all`** (new) — `auth.RemoveAllContexts` removes every context, its keyring token, and **all cluster bindings** — a true "log me out everywhere." The `Long` help explains the distinction.

This is the honest split: the default is precise about what it did, and there's a one-shot escape hatch for full logout. (Worth noting `File.Delete` already strips the *logged-out* context's own bindings, so the only thing surviving a default logout is genuinely the *other* accounts — which is exactly what the note now surfaces.)

## 1. Synthetic protocol-level tests — **we vendored these; they run in our suite**
The `internal/remotehelper/*` packages ship with extensive table/fuzz/fault tests that drive the helper protocol against an in-process `httptest` server and assert wire shapes (pkt-line framing, capability negotiation, agent injection, failover, redaction). Counts in our copy:

- `transport` — 45 (proxy/inforefs, fault injection)
- `gitproto` — 20 (+ fuzz)
- plus `httpdebug`, `replicas`, `debuglog`

These came across when I vendored and **pass in `mise run test`** — so the CLI has solid protocol-level coverage.

## 2. Real-binary-against-real-server e2e — **in entiredb only, NOT vendored**
`test/git_remote_entire_test.go` (`TestGitRemoteEntire`) and `test/git_remote_entire_shallow_test.go` (`TestGitRemoteEntire_ShallowDepth1Clone`) spin up a **real entire-server** (`testserver.SetupTestEnv`), provision a repo, and run the **actual `git` binary** through `git-remote-entire` against `entire://` URLs — full clone/push, and the shallow `--depth 1` smoke test. They depend on entiredb's server + storage + `gittest` infra, so they **can't run in the CLI repo**.

## What this means for our PR
- The shallow-fetch port I just did (`3e8f6d6d7`) is exactly what `TestGitRemoteEntire_ShallowDepth1Clone` guards — and that test lives upstream, not here. So the CLI has **no real end-to-end clone/push/shallow test**; we rely on (a) the vendored synthetic tests and (b) the fact it's a verbatim port of upstream-tested code.
- That's a genuine coverage gap worth noting: to truly e2e-test `git clone entire://` from the CLI side, we'd need either to run against a live/dev entire-server (like `mise run dev` provides in the devenv) or to vendor a lightweight server fixture — neither of which exists in the CLI repo today.
